ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample Complexity of KernelSHAP Estimator
PROPOSAL: Analyze the sample complexity of KernelSHAP in terms of achieving a desired level of approximation to the true Shapley values. Specifically, prove a non-asymptotic bound on the number of samples required for a KernelSHAP estimator to approximate the Shapley values within a certain error threshold, using techniques from high-probability concentration inequalities and worst-case analysis.
CONTROLS: Adapt the bound to account for different kernel functions and sampling distributions, including comparison to LeverageSHAP's worst-case bounds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The result should establish a maximum sample size that KernelSHAP requires to achieve a certain level of accuracy, and potentially reveal limitations of the estimator in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: LeverageSHAP vs. KernelSHAP: Experimental Comparison
PROPOSAL: Conduct a head-to-head comparison of the performance of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP on a suite of benchmark datasets from different domains (e.g., computer vision, natural language processing, finance), using metrics such as estimated Shapley values, statistical significance of differences between feature contributions, and user study ratings of explanation quality.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP under different sampling distributions (e.g., uniform, weighted by kernel function), and evaluate the effect of dataset size and dimensionality on the relative performance of the two estimators.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: The experimental comparison should shed light on the strengths and weaknesses of each estimator, and reveal whether LeverageSHAP's statistical leverage sampling schedule provides a significant advantage over KernelSHAP's random sampling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Explanation for Non-Linear Interactions
PROPOSAL: Extend the Shapley value framework to capture non-linear interactions between features, by incorporating interaction terms into the value function v(S) and developing a novel kernel-based estimator that can accurately estimate these interactions.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the new estimator on datasets where non-linear interactions are significant, and compare it to existing methods that only capture linear interactions (e.g., KernelSHAP).
COST: 16500
PREDICTION: The new estimator should provide more accurate explanations for data points with non-linear feature interactions, but may require larger sample sizes or more computationally expensive kernel evaluations to achieve acceptable accuracy.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: LeverageSHAP vs. KernelSHAP: Experimental Comparison
PROPOSAL: To further investigate the relative performance of LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP, design and implement a set of ablation studies that evaluate the impact of different factors on the performance of each estimator. For example, compare the effect of sampling without replacement, paired sampling, and uniform sampling on the accuracy of each estimator, and analyze the trade-off between sample efficiency and accuracy.
CONTROLS: Use the same benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics as before, and add additional metrics to assess the robustness of each estimator to variations in the sampling distribution.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: The ablation studies should provide a more nuanced understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of each estimator, and reveal the key factors that contribute to their relative performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Shapley Value Estimation for High-Dimensional Data using Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop a method for estimating Shapley values in high-dimensional data by leveraging transfer learning from lower-dimensional data. Specifically, train a model on a lower-dimensional dataset and then use this model as a feature extractor to reduce the dimensionality of the high-dimensional data, after which apply Shapley value estimation to the reduced data.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the method on high-dimensional datasets with varying levels of sparsity and correlation, and compare it to existing methods for high-dimensional Shapley value estimation.
COST: 23320
PREDICTION: The transfer learning approach should provide a more efficient and accurate method for estimating Shapley values in high-dimensional data, but may require careful selection of the lower-dimensional dataset and model architecture to achieve good results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Framework for Model-Agnostic Explanation via Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified framework for estimating Shapley values that can work with a wide range of models, including linear and non-linear models, and can handle both low-dimensional and high-dimensional data. The framework should be based on a novel combination of techniques from kernel methods, transfer learning, and optimization.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the framework on a diverse set of datasets and models, and compare it to existing methods for model-agnostic explanation.
COST: 45000
PREDICTION: The unified framework should provide a powerful and flexible tool for estimating Shapley values, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and selection of appropriate kernel and transfer learning methods to achieve good results.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Shapley Value Estimation for High-Dimensional Data using Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: To further improve the transfer learning method for high-dimensional data, investigate the use of adversarial training to robustify the feature extractor against perturbations in the input data. This could help improve the stability and reliability of the Shapley value estimates in high-dimensional spaces.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the adversarial training method on high-dimensional datasets with varying levels of sparsity and correlation, and compare it to existing methods for high-dimensional Shapley value estimation.
COST: 54000
PREDICTION: The adversarial training method should help improve the robustness of the transfer learning approach, but may require careful selection of hyperparameters and training schedules to achieve good results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Explaining Model Uncertainty through Conditional Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Extend the Shapley value framework to explain not only the contribution of individual features to the expected model output, but also the contribution of features to the uncertainty of the model output. This can be achieved by developing conditional Shapley values that capture the expected value and variance of the model output given different subsets of features.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the conditional Shapley values on datasets with varying levels of model uncertainty, and compare it to existing methods for explaining model uncertainty.
COST: 75000
PREDICTION: The conditional Shapley values should provide a more comprehensive understanding of model behavior and uncertainty, but may require careful selection of hyperparameters and evaluation metrics to achieve good results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable and Efficient Computation of Shapley Values using Approximation Algorithms
PROPOSAL: Develop approximation algorithms for computing Shapley values that can scale to large datasets and high-dimensional feature spaces. This can be achieved through a combination of techniques from approximation algorithms, combinatorial optimization, and machine learning.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the approximation algorithms on large datasets and compare it to exact methods and existing approximation algorithms.
COST: 113200
PREDICTION: The approximation algorithms should provide a significant speedup for computing Shapley values, but may require careful selection of hyperparameters and approximation thresholds to achieve good results and trade off between accuracy and efficiency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Fairness of Shapley-based Explanations
PROPOSAL: Investigate the fairness of explanations obtained through Shapley values, specifically in the context of sensitive attributes such as race, gender, and socio-economic status. This can be achieved through a combination of fairness metrics, bias analysis, and human evaluation studies.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the fairness of Shapley-based explanations on datasets with sensitive attributes and compare it to explanations obtained through other methods.
COST: 150000
PREDICTION: The fairness evaluation should provide insights into the limitations and potential biases of Shapley-based explanations, but may require careful selection of fairness metrics and evaluation protocols to achieve meaningful results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Long-Term Temporal Consistency in Satellites Images with a Large-Scale Modality-Specific Pre-Training
PROPOSAL: We pretrain our model on a large-scale dataset of satellite images with a focus on modality-specific objectives for remote sensing, such as change detection, image classification, and depth estimation. This pre-training stage will encourage our model to understand the low-level and mid-level image patterns specific to satellite images, making it well-prepared to learn arbitrary complex patterns.
CONTROLS:_baseline consists of a standard transformer model pre-trained on a generic multimodal dataset and MDETR pre-trained on the same remote sensing dataset but without any modality-specific objectives.
COST: 28800
PREDICTION: Our approach should significantly outperform baselines, especially in remote sensing tasks that emphasize understanding low-level image patterns. Failure may occur when the real-world data varies significantly from what's seen in the pre-training stage.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporally Consistent Future Satellite Image Forecasting with a change-Aware Encoder-Decoder Model
PROPOSAL: We propose a change-aware encoder-decoder model that employs a novel change-aware encoding mechanism. This mechanism captures the change patterns in the input sequence of historical images, allowing the decoder to generate a temporally consistent future image. The change-aware encoding is learned through a novel change-reconstruction loss term that incentivizes the model to understand the underlying reasons for the changes.
CONTROLS: ablate the model by removing the change-aware encoding mechanism, compare with a standard encoder-decoder model that predicts the future image directly from the input sequence without considering the change patterns.
COST: 43200
PREDICTION: Our proposed change-aware encoder-decoder model should significantly outperform the ablated and standard models in predicting temporally consistent future satellite images. Failure may occur when the future changes are significantly more complex or nuanced than what's seen in the historical data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting with a Filtering-based Metric
PROPOSAL: We propose a filtering-based metric to evaluate the temporal consistency of future satellite image forecasts. The metric applies a series of filters to the predicted future images, simulating the observation process of a satellite imaging system, and measures the degradation of the forecast quality over time. This metric will allow us to rigorously assess the temporal consistency of different forecasting models.
CONTROLS: compare the proposed metric with standard image quality metrics (e.g., PSNR, SSIM) and visually evaluate the quality of the predicted future images.
COST: 54000
PREDICTION: Our proposed metric should provide a more accurate and nuanced evaluation of temporal consistency, revealing differences between forecasting models that standard metrics miss. However, the implementation of the metric may be computationally expensive, leading to potential performance issues for large-scale forecasting tasks.

ACTION: REVISE
2. Temporally Consistent Future Satellite Image Forecasting with a change-Aware Encoder-Decoder Model
TITLE: Temporally Consistent Future Satellite Image Forecasting with a change-Aware Encoder-Decoder Model: A Deeper Look into Change Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We explore the change reconstruction mechanism in our change-aware encoder-decoder model and propose modifications to improve its ability to capture complex change patterns. Specifically, we add a temporal convolutional block to the change reconstruction head to aggregate information from the entire input sequence, and a self-supervised loss function to encourage the model to learn multiple modes of change.
CONTROLS: ablate the modified change reconstruction head by removing the temporal convolutional block and the self-supervised loss function, compare with the original model.
COST: 72000
PREDICTION: The modified change reconstruction mechanism should improve the model's ability to capture complex change patterns, leading to more accurate and temporally consistent future image forecasts. However, the increased complexity of the model may lead to overfitting if not carefully regularized.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Input Sequence Length on Temporally Consistent Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We conduct an extensive study on the effect of input sequence length on the performance of temporally consistent future satellite image forecasting models. We explore different sequence lengths, from a short sequence of 2 images to a long sequence of 12 images, and evaluate the models' performance under different settings using metrics such as filtering-based metric and change reconstruction loss.
CONTROLS: evaluate the models' performance under different sequence lengths, compare with baseline models that are not specifically designed for long sequence lengths.
COST: 129600
PREDICTION: Our study should provide a deeper understanding of the effect of input sequence length on the performance of future satellite image forecasting models, and inform the design of future models that can handle varying sequence lengths. However, the computational cost of training and evaluating models under different sequence lengths may be prohibitively expensive for extremely long sequences.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for Temporal Change Description and Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-task learning framework that trains a single model to perform both temporal change description and future satellite image forecasting tasks simultaneously. The model will be trained on a shared representation learned from a large-scale modality-specific pre-training stage, and will be supervised by both change description and forecasting losses.
CONTROLS: compare the proposed multi-task learning framework with single-task learning approaches, ablate the model by removing one of the tasks.
COST: 173200
PREDICTION: The proposed multi-task learning framework should improve the performance of both tasks by sharing knowledge and regularizing the representation learning, but may suffer from task interference or competing objectives if not carefully designed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Transfer Learning for Generalizing to New Regions and Observation Conditions
PROPOSAL: We propose an adversarial transfer learning method that fine-tunes the pre-trained model on a new region or observation condition while an adversarial generator tries to confuse the model, encouraging it to learn more generalized and robust features. This method aims to improve the model's ability to generalize to new regions and observation conditions.
CONTROLS: compare the proposed adversarial transfer learning method with standard fine-tuning approaches, evaluate the method on different scenarios such as transfer to new regions, seasons, or sensor modalities.
COST: 259200
PREDICTION: The proposed adversarial transfer learning method should improve the model's generalization ability to new regions and observation conditions, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and may not always succeed in extracting robust features.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Human Evaluation of Temporal Consistency in Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We conduct a human evaluation study to assess the temporal consistency of future satellite image forecasts generated by different models. A group of volunteers will be shown a set of forecasted images and will be asked to rate their temporal consistency in relation to the actual future image.
CONTROLS: compare the human evaluation ratings with the predictions made by automated metrics, evaluate the inter-rater agreement among the volunteers.
COST: 388800
PREDICTION: The human evaluation study should provide a more nuanced understanding of temporal consistency and its relationship with automated metrics, but may be limited by the subjectivity of human ratings and the inter-rater variability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Change Description as a Regularization Term for Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose to use temporal change description as a regularization term for future satellite image forecasting. The idea is to incorporate the task of change description into the forecasting task, and use the change description loss as a regularization term to improve the forecasting model's performance.
CONTROLS: compare the proposed regularization approach with standard regularization techniques, ablate the model by removing the change description regularization term.
COST: 580000
PREDICTION: The proposed regularization approach should improve the forecasting model's performance and temporal consistency, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and may not always succeed in incorporating the change description task effectively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable and Efficient Inference for Temporally Consistent Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel method for scalable and efficient inference for temporally consistent future satellite image forecasting. The method utilizes a neural architecture search to discover an efficient and accurate inference pipeline, and a batch processing technique to parallelize the inference process.
CONTROLS: compare the proposed method with standard inference methods, ablate the model by removing the neural architecture search stage or the batch processing stage.
COST: 864000
PREDICTION: The proposed method should improve the inference efficiency and scalability of temporally consistent future satellite image forecasting, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and may not always succeed in discovering an optimal inference pipeline.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Adapter Sizes on Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of online time series forecasting models with different adapter sizes (e.g., 1-layer MLP, 2-layer MLP, convnet) in traffic flow forecasting and electricity consumption forecasting datasets, using offline updates on collected data and online updates with incremental data. Evaluate the model's ability to adapt to concept drift and changes in the data distribution.
CONTROLS: compare with the original model without an adapter, and ablate the adapter by freezing its parameters while updating the base model.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: Larger adapters will generally perform better, especially when the data distribution changes significantly, but may also adapt more slowly due to increased model complexity. Online updates could reduce this adaptation speed disparity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Parameter Update Strategies on Delayed Feedback
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of online time series forecasting models with different parameter update strategies (e.g., batch gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, gradient clipping, skip connections) when dealing with delayed feedback in multi-step forecasting tasks, specifically in the weather forecasting and solar power forecasting datasets. Evaluate the model's ability to adapt to changing conditions despite delayed and noisy feedback.
CONTROLS: compare with the baseline of using OGD and ablate the update strategies one by one to understand their effects.
COST: 9600
PREDICTION: Gradient clipping and skip connections will help stabilize the updates and improve performance in the presence of delayed feedback, but may introduce additional training time costs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Normalization and Adaptation in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the impact of normalization techniques (e.g., batch normalization, layer normalization, instance normalization) combined with adaptation mechanisms (e.g., adapter modules, ensemble methods) on the performance of online time series forecasting models in real-world datasets. Specifically, use electricity consumption forecasting and exchange rate forecasting datasets, and develop a framework that incorporates both normalization and adaptation mechanisms for improved performance.
CONTROLS: compare with standard normalization techniques (e.g., standardization, feature scaling) and ablate the adaptation mechanisms.
COST: 12960
PREDICTION: Combining normalization and adaptation mechanisms will lead to better performance and robustness, particularly when dealing with concept drift and changes in the data distribution.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Normalization and Adaptation in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: REVISE the proposal to focus specifically on how different normalization techniques affect the stability and robustness of online adaptation mechanisms, by analyzing the sensitivity of the optimization process to the choice of normalization layer (e.g., batch vs. layer vs. instance norm) in the presence of adaptation mechanisms (e.g., adapter modules). Use the traffic flow forecasting dataset and compare with standard normalization techniques as controls.
CONTROLS: ablate the normalization techniques to understand their effects on the adaptation mechanisms.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: Instance normalization will lead to more stable updates and better robustness to changing conditions, due to its ability to normalize the data distribution at the individual sample level, rather than the batch or feature level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Exploration-Exploitation Trade-Offs in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of online time series forecasting models with different exploration-exploitation trade-offs (e.g., epsilon-greedy, upper confidence bound, entropy-based exploration) when applied to real-world datasets, specifically in the context of electricity consumption forecasting, exchange rate forecasting, and traffic flow forecasting. Evaluate the model's ability to balance exploration and exploitation in the presence of delayed feedback and concept drift.
CONTROLS: compare with a baseline that does not incorporate exploration-exploitation trade-offs and ablate the trade-off mechanisms.
COST: 19440
PREDICTION: The performance of online forecasting models will be significantly improved by incorporating exploration-exploitation trade-offs, particularly in high-noise or high-delay scenarios, but may require careful tuning to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Role of Data Reuse in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of online time series forecasting models that reuse different amounts of historical data (e.g., experience replay, data caching, temporal ensembling) when applied to real-world datasets, specifically in the context of traffic flow forecasting and solar power forecasting. Evaluate the model's ability to learn from past experiences and adapt to changing conditions in the presence of delayed feedback and concept drift.
CONTROLS: compare with a baseline that does not reuse historical data and ablate the amount of reused data.
COST: 25920
PREDICTION: Reusing historical data will lead to improved performance and robustness in online time series forecasting, particularly in scenarios with high concept drift or delayed feedback, but may require careful tuning to balance the trade-off between data reuse and model stability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Theoretical Framework for Dynamic Regret Analysis in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to analyze the dynamic regret of online time series forecasting algorithms in the presence of delayed feedback and concept drift. Derive bounds on the dynamic regret for different classes of algorithms (e.g., stochastic gradient descent, online gradient descent, adaptive algorithms) and explore the trade-offs between exploration and exploitation, model adaptation, and data reuse.
CONTROLS: assume theoretical models for the concepts of delayed feedback and concept drift.
COST: 38880
PREDICTION: The developed framework will provide insights into the underlying trade-offs between exploration, exploitation, model adaptation, and data reuse in online time series forecasting, and help understand why certain algorithms perform better than others in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing the Performance of State-Space Models and Deep Learning Architectures in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of state-space models (e.g., Kalman filter, particle filter) and deep learning architectures (e.g., LSTM, GRU) in online time series forecasting tasks, focusing on their ability to adapt to changing conditions, handle delayed feedback, and capture complex dynamics in traffic flow forecasting and electricity consumption forecasting datasets.
CONTROLS: compare with a baseline that uses a pre-trained deep learning model and ablate the model architecture.
COST: 51840
PREDICTION: State-space models will perform well in scenarios with mild concept drift and delayed feedback, while deep learning architectures will excel in scenarios with complex dynamics and rapid concept drift, due to their ability to learn non-linear relationships and adapt to changing conditions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Effect of Heteroscedasticity on Online Time Series Forecasting Algorithms
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of heteroscedasticity (non-constant variance) on online time series forecasting algorithms, specifically in the context of traffic flow forecasting and solar power forecasting datasets with varying levels of heteroscedasticity. Evaluate the performance of different algorithms when faced with heteroscedasticity and compare their sensitivity to changes in the variance of the data.
CONTROLS: compare with a baseline that assumes homoscedasticity and ablate the effect of heteroscedasticity on different algorithms.
COST: 77760
PREDICTION: Algorithms that are robust to heteroscedasticity will outperform those that are not, particularly in scenarios with rapidly changing variance, and techniques that account for heteroscedasticity (e.g., weighted regression, conditional variance estimation) will improve forecasting accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Case Studies of Online Time Series Forecasting in Real-World Applications
PROPOSAL: Apply the insights and algorithms developed throughout this series of experiments to real-world applications in traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, and weather forecasting, using real-world datasets and deployment settings to evaluate the practical impact of the proposed methods.
CONTROLS: use the same datasets and deployment settings used in the experimental evaluations to ensure realistic comparison.
COST: 155520
PREDICTION: The online time series forecasting algorithms and techniques developed in this series will demonstrate real-world impact and improve forecasting accuracy, robustness, and adaptability in various domains, and will also provide a foundation for future research and applications in the field.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lightweight Dense Text Retriever for Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
We compare the performance of a state-of-the-art ColPali-based vision-centric retriever with a hybrid retrieval approach that combines the ColPali retriever with a lightweight dense text retriever. Specifically, we train a mini-BERT-based retriever on a subset of the underlying documents, reducing the representation dimensionality to 128 and choosing the query/document batch size and number of transformer layers to minimize latency while maintaining reasonable performance. The performance of this hybrid approach will be evaluated over a subset of public benchmarks, with the specific focus on reducing latency and improving the trade-off between retrieval quality and online latency.
CONTROLS: Compare the ColPali-based retriever with BM25 and mini-BERT-based retriever without ColPali
COST: 32400
PREDICTION: Our results will likely show that the hybrid retrieval approach improves the trade-off between retrieval quality and online latency compared with scaling up the ColPali-based retriever alone, and the lightweight dense text retriever might still slightly improve performance compared to BM25. However, this success might fail without reducing the model dimensionality and other latency parameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Aggregated Similarity Scores for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
We explore methods for aggregating the similarity scores of individual retrievers in a hybrid retrieval setup. Specifically, we propose to first normalize the scores of each retriever (i.e., ColPali-based vision-centric retriever and lightweight dense text retriever) based on their internal distributions, then combine them using a scaled sum or element-wise product, and apply a softmax function on the aggregated scores to obtain the final probabilities. The performance of these methods will be evaluated on various visual document retrieval benchmarks, including both early interaction and late interaction variants.
CONTROLS: Compare the scaled sum and element-wise product with a simple sum or average, without any normalization
COST: 54000
PREDICTION: Our results will likely show that the scaled sum and element-wise product significantly improve the performance of the hybrid retrieval approach, especially in scenarios where the text retriever is weak but still somewhat complementary to the vision-centric retriever.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED: Aggregated Similarity Scores for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
We explore methods for aggregating the similarity scores of individual retrievers in a hybrid retrieval setup. Specifically, we propose to use a learnable weight-sharing neural network to fuse the similarity scores of the ColPali-based vision-centric retriever and the lightweight dense text retriever. This network will take the concatenated scores as input and output the final probability scores, while sharing learnable weights across different scores. The performance of this method will be evaluated on various visual document retrieval benchmarks, including both early interaction and late interaction variants.
CONTROLS: Compare with the scaled sum and element-wise product methods proposed in rev 2, and also without any aggregation method (i.e., simply use the ColPali-based retriever's scores or lightweight text retriever's scores)
COST: 64800
PREDICTION: Our results will likely show that the learnable weight-sharing neural network-based fusion significantly improves the performance of the hybrid retrieval approach, especially in scenarios where the scores of individual retrievers are highly complementary but have different distributions. However, if the complements are not strong, the overhead of this method may hinder its practicality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Aggregation of Heterogeneous Representations
PROPOSAL: 
To efficiently aggregate the representations of heterogeneous retrievers in a hybrid setup, we propose to use a novel, architecture-agnostic method based on the Eigendecomposition of the concatenated representation space. This method enables a rotation of the representations of individual retrievers to a shared space, reducing intra-retriever similarities while highlighting inter-retriever complementarity. We then employ a simple sum or scaled sum of the projected representations to obtain the aggregated representation. The performance of this method will be evaluated on various visual document retrieval benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Compare with the learnable weight-sharing neural network-based fusion method from rev 2, and also with the standard late-interaction method used in ColPali-based retrievers
COST: 77400
PREDICTION: Our results will likely show that the Eigendecomposition-based aggregation method significantly improves the performance of the hybrid retrieval approach, especially in scenarios where the representations of individual retrievers have vastly different structures, while keeping latency low due to the simple nature of the method. However, this method may fail in more complex aggregation scenarios or when a large number of heterogeneous retrievers are involved.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Batch-wise Aggregation for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
To further improve the efficiency of the hybrid retrieval approach, we propose to aggregate the representations of individual retrievers in batch-wise manner, rather than for individual query-document pairs. Specifically, we first compute the aggregated representations for each batch of queries and documents, then use these aggregated representations for ranking. We explore different batch aggregation methods, including simple average and scaled average, and evaluate their performance on various visual document retrieval benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Compare with the Eigendecomposition-based aggregation method from proposal 3, and also with a baseline that aggregates representations for individual query-document pairs
COST: 97200
PREDICTION: Our results will likely show that the batch-wise aggregation method achieves significant latency improvements while maintaining comparable performance to the Eigendecomposition-based aggregation method. However, it may have some compromises on memory usage due to the need to store batch-wise aggregated representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning to Adapt the Aggregate Representation for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to learn an adaptive mechanism to adjust the aggregate representation computed from the batch-wise aggregation method or Eigendecomposition-based aggregation method. Specifically, we use a learnable attention mechanism to dynamically weight individual representations from different retrievers, and aggregate these weights to obtain the final aggregate representation. We use a contrastive learning objective to train the attention mechanism to improve the discriminability of the aggregate representation. The performance of this method will be evaluated on various visual document retrieval benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Compare with the standard late-interaction method used in ColPali-based retrievers and the batch-wise aggregation method from proposal 4, and also without the adaptive attention mechanism (i.e., use a fixed weight for all representations)
COST: 120960
PREDICTION: Our results will likely show that the adaptive attention mechanism significantly improves the performance of the hybrid retrieval approach, especially in cases where the representations of individual retrievers have vastly different levels of importance. However, this method may fail if the contrastive learning objective is not properly aligned with the ranking objective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Incorporating Auxiliary Tasks for Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
To leverage the strengths of both text and vision-centric retrievers, we propose to incorporate auxiliary tasks into the training process of the hybrid retrieval approach. Specifically, we add tasks such as text-based document classification, visual-based zero-shot classification, and query paraphrasing to the standard ranking objective. We explore different types of auxiliary losses, including cross-entropy loss, triplet loss, and similarity loss, and evaluate their performance on various visual document retrieval benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Compare with the adaptive attention mechanism from proposal 5, and also without any auxiliary tasks (i.e., use only the standard ranking objective)
COST: 155520
PREDICTION: Our results will likely show that incorporating auxiliary tasks significantly improves the performance of the hybrid retrieval approach, especially in cases where the auxiliary tasks are complementary to the ranking objective. However, this method may fail if the auxiliary tasks are too complex or if the ranking objective is not properly aligned with the auxiliary tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Generalizability of Hybrid Retrieval Approaches
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to evaluate the generalizability of the hybrid retrieval approaches by testing their performance on unseen domains, datasets, and scenarios. Specifically, we will train the hybrid retrieval models on one or more domains and evaluate their performance on a different domain, dataset, or scenario. We will also explore methods for domain adaptation, such as knowledge distillation, adversarial training, and self-supervised learning, to improve the generalizability of the hybrid retrieval approaches.
CONTROLS: Compare with the standard late-interaction method used in ColPali-based retrievers, and also with the hybrid retrieval approaches proposed in previous experiments (with and without domain adaptation methods)
COST: 190080
PREDICTION: Our results will likely show that the hybrid retrieval approaches have better generalizability than the standard late-interaction method, especially when domain adaptation methods are used. However, the effectiveness of these methods may vary depending on the specific domain and scenario.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Visual Document Retrieval with Exemplar-Based Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to integrate exemplar-based learning into the hybrid retrieval framework. Specifically, we will learn a set of exemplars for each document in the training set, and then use these exemplars to aggregate the representations of individual retrievers. We will explore different methods for learning exemplars, such as self-supervised learning and unsupervised clustering, and evaluate their performance on various visual document retrieval benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Compare with the adaptive attention mechanism from proposal 5, and also with the hybrid retrieval approaches proposed in previous experiments (with and without exemplar-based learning)
COST: 240000
PREDICTION: Our results will likely show that the exemplar-based hybrid retrieval approach significantly improves the performance of the hybrid retrieval framework, especially in cases where the exemplars effectively capture the distinct features of each document. However, the effectiveness of this method may vary depending on the specific datasets and retrieval tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Deployment and Efficiency Analysis of Hybrid Retrieval Approaches
PROPOSAL: 
We propose to perform a thorough deployment and efficiency analysis of the hybrid retrieval approaches proposed in this study. Specifically, we will analyze the latency, throughput, and resource utilization of each approach on various hardware configurations and evaluate their performance in a real-world deployment setting. We will also explore methods for optimizing the efficiency of the hybrid retrieval approaches, such as selecting the most relevant retrievers for each query and document, and caching frequently accessed retriever outputs.
